about: Parallel edges and self-loops, the two cases a style generator gets wrong. Grouping is by unordered node pair, so the four edges between p and q are one group of four however they are directed: e0 p->q, e2 q->p, e3 p->q, e5 q->p. The r-s pair is interleaved with it on purpose — e1 and e4 sit between the p-q edges — so a fan that read the groups as one contiguous run per endpoint would call r-s two groups of one and give both its edges no offset. That interleaving is the whole reason the fan is two chained counting sorts rather than one. t carries two self-loops, which are a parallel group of their own and whose fan moves the loop's centre rather than a perpendicular chord. u->p is a group of one, so it must take no offset at all. Node order is interleaved with edge order on purpose: p, r, q, s, t, u, so the lower dense index of a pair is not always its first edge's source.
